subtype: Approach: trying to relearn everything from scratch [Pitfall]
passage: Devika opened her history book to Chapter 1 on the first evening of the last month before the board exams, then did the same with science, maths and civics. "Basics first," she told herself, and copied out the early chapters in neat handwriting. On Friday in the school library, Sahil saw three books open to early chapters. "Isn't it week three?" he asked. She checked her planner. History had reached Chapter 8 of 15, maths Chapter 7 of 14, and she had not touched the last chapters of any book. "Those carry the most marks," Sahil said quietly, holding his own list of high-mark chapters. Devika counted the days left: nine. Her stomach dropped, and the bell rang before she could answer.

qa.q: Which chapter of history had Devika reached by week three?
What was Devika feeling as she counted the days left?
qa.a: Devika felt alarmed and dismayed; her stomach dropped when she saw how much of the syllabus was still untouched. 😰

qa.q: What different approach could Devika use for the last nine days, and why would it help?
qa.a: She could rank chapters by marks and do the heavily weighted last chapters first, revising earlier ones only where she has gaps, because time is short and those chapters carry the most marks.

qa.q: How does Sahil see Devika's plan?
qa.a: Sahil sees a hardworking classmate spending scarce days at the wrong end of the books, so he gently points out the high-mark chapters from his own list.

grounding: The student restarts every book from Chapter 1, finishes only about half the syllabus by week three, and leaves the heavily weighted final chapters untouched.

subtype: Approach: trying to relearn everything from scratch [Pitfall]
passage:
Dear Ishita,
You asked how revision's going, and I'm going to be honest because I need someone to know. On 1 February I decided to start every book from Chapter 1 and go properly, page by page, so nothing would be missed. It felt so responsible. It's now the third week. In Chemistry I'm on chapter 7 of 15. Physics, chapter 6 of 14. Maths is a bit better. And the chapters at the end, electrochemistry, optics, probability, are exactly the ones Sir says carry the most marks. I haven't touched them. I keep rereading things I already knew from Class 11, because stopping feels like skipping. The exam is in nine days. What did you do? Please write back soon.
Vidya

qa.q: Which Chemistry chapter has Vidya reached?
How is Vidya feeling as the exam gets closer?
qa.a: Vidya feels anxious and stuck, with the heaviest chapters untouched and only nine days left, and needs someone to know.

qa.q: What would you change first in Vidya's plan?
qa.a: Jump straight to the high-mark final chapters like electrochemistry, optics and probability, and only skim the Class 11 material already known.

qa.q: How might Ishita feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Ishita may feel worried for Vidya and want to reply quickly with practical help, since the letter asks directly.

grounding: A student's letter shows restarting every book from Chapter 1, so by week three the heavily weighted final chapters are untouched.

subtype: Approach: trying to relearn everything from scratch [Pitfall]
passage: Ojas, you're starting from Chapter 1 again? Stop. Let me tell you what happened to me. I'm Ritu, and two years ago, with a month left, I did exactly that. Every book, page one. I told myself it was thorough. By week three I was barely halfway through Biology. The last units, genetics and ecology, carry a huge chunk of the paper, and I hadn't opened them. In the last four days I tried to do both. I was reading genetics at two in the morning, remembering nothing. In the exam I left most of one long answer blank. I knew chapter 1 of every book perfectly. Nobody asked much about chapter 1. So please, look at the marks first, then decide where to start.

qa.q: Which Biology units had Ritu not opened by week three?
How might Ritu have felt reading genetics at two in the morning?
qa.a: Ritu was probably panicked and exhausted, trying to cram heavy units with no time left.

qa.q: What would have been a better starting point for Ritu?
qa.a: Checking which units carried the most marks first and revising genetics and ecology early, while only skimming chapters already known.

qa.q: How might Ojas feel hearing the story?
qa.a: Ojas may feel a bit caught out but grateful, since the warning comes from someone who made exactly the same mistake.

grounding: A student tells how restarting every book from Chapter 1 left heavily weighted final units hurried and a long answer blank.
